purpose: Qualitative demand/friction intelligence for the single Stödassistenten learning system. Scores are ordinal discovery priorities, not measured search volumes or eligibility evidence. Housing-adaptation owner-role rules are truth-bearing only after current primary-source verification; natural-language queries are discovery patterns, never factual sources.

scoring.priority_rule: Prioritize combinations of high demand, high friction, high consequence and weak current product coverage. These scores guide eval, retrieval and question-order work only.

natural_language_queries: vi sitter i brf-styrelsen och en medlem behöver ramp vem ska söka bidraget
kan brf ta över bostadsanpassningsbidraget för entrén
vem ansvarar för anpassningen om föreningen tar över bidraget
kan föreningen få reparationsbidrag eller återställningsbidrag senare

demand_signal.basis: Housing adaptation in multifamily buildings repeatedly involves residents plus landlords or housing associations, creating a recurring owner-side information need. The score is qualitative prioritization, not measured query volume.

friction_signal.basis: Consent, initial applicant status, optional takeover, common-area scope, payment, repair and restoration are separate legal/process concepts that are easy to collapse into one 'the BRF applies' assumption.

miss_consequence.basis: Wrong routing can make the resident or owner start with the wrong applicant, use takeover for an in-apartment measure, miss required written evidence or make incorrect assumptions about later repair/restoration support.

source_fragmentation.basis: The safe route spans current Boverket pages on owner consent, takeover, payment and restoration rather than one single rule or form.

language_accessibility_friction.basis: Terms such as sökande, fastighetsägare, medgivande, övertagande, kontantbidrag, reparation and återställning are process-heavy and can obscure who does what next.

steps_to_action.basis: A useful answer first needs only a few high-information distinctions: inside apartment versus common area, whether a positive cash-grant decision already exists, and whether the parties are considering consent only or a voluntary takeover.

recurrence_signal.basis: The role confusion is structurally recurring whenever an adaptation affects entrances, stairwells, laundry rooms or other shared parts of a multifamily building. This is a qualitative recurrence signal.

current_product_coverage_gap.basis: The product already protects the resident/tenant side of housing adaptation but the feedback coverage and public actor entry lacked a dedicated coarse property-actor context, leaving BRF/landlord users with a weaker journey.

signals.recommended_learning_action: Add a public coarse BRF/property entry into the existing shared product, preserve actor-segmented anonymous feedback, ask only common-area/decision-stage/takeover facts that can change the process, and lock the owner-role distinction as a permanent synthetic regression.
signals.truth_rule: Verify current owner-consent, takeover, repair and restoration rules against Boverket and the responsible municipality; do not infer eligibility, applicant status, takeover validity or later grant rights from the actor label alone.
